name: Pulmonary Neoplasm
description: A neoplastic growth involving lung tissue. Pulmonary neoplasms may be benign or malignant, but persistent or suspicious pulmonary lesions and associated respiratory or systemic symptoms require evaluation to determine pathology and, when malignant, stage.
physical_examination: Examination may be non-specific or normal in early disease
Assessment for abnormal or reduced breath sounds
Assessment for weight loss or cachexia
Assessment for signs of metastatic or locally advanced disease when clinically suspected
recommended_investigations: Chest imaging, typically including diagnostic chest CT
Tissue biopsy when malignancy is suspected
Bronchoscopy or image-guided sampling depending on lesion location
Staging evaluation when malignancy is confirmed
red_flags: Progressive or severe shortness of breath
New neurologic symptoms suggesting metastatic disease
Facial or neck swelling suggesting major thoracic vascular obstruction
contraindications: Do not treat a model label of pulmonary neoplasm as confirmed cancer; definitive diagnosis requires appropriate clinical and pathologic evaluation.
